cards.explanation: The answer is persuade them. Paul writes, "…we try to persuade men." Persuading means talking with people, not pushing them around. I think that's a gentle way to treat anyone you care about. And notice he says "try," which makes me feel better about the cookies I try to stamp straight.

The answer is appearances. Paul writes that some take pride in appearances rather than in the heart. Appearances are like a cookie that looks perfect on top and is raw dough in the middle. Pretty on the outside, nothing going on inside. Paul wants the Corinthians to be able to answer them.

The answer is the Corinthians. Paul writes, "if we are of sound mind, it is for you." The "you" is the church in Corinth, the people he's writing to (2 Corinthians 1:1). So being out of their mind is for God, and being of sound mind is for the Corinthians. I think that's a pretty generous way to describe your own behavior.

The answer is Christ's love. Paul writes, "…Christ’s love compels us…" Compels is a strong word, like being pressed to act. I think that's the difference between a job you're handed and being moved by Christ's love.

The answer is themselves. Paul writes that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again. Living for yourself is a very small kitchen to bake in. The verse points you toward Christ instead. Notice that it says He was raised again, so the One they live for is alive.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer." So there was a time they regarded Christ according to the flesh. Now they don't. That's a real change in how they see Him.

The answer is that the old has passed away. Paul writes, "The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" It doesn't say the old got a patch or a polish. It says it passed away. That's good news for anybody tired of being the old version of themselves.

The answer is trespasses. Paul writes that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, "…not counting men’s trespasses against them." God isn't keeping a tally against them. Think of a big sheet of paper where the marks aren't being added up. That's good news for anyone who feels like their list is long.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "…He has committed to us the message of reconciliation." God put the message into their hands. I think that's quite a thing to be trusted with. It's even bigger than being trusted with the good cookie sheet.

The answer is ambassadors for Christ. Paul writes, "…we are ambassadors for Christ…" An ambassador speaks for the one who sent him, and he doesn't make up his own message. Paul adds that it's "…as though God were making His appeal through us." So he and the people with him carry Christ's message.

The answer is reconciled. Paul writes, "We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God." Implore is a strong word, like a plea. I think you only plead like that when you really want someone to say yes. This is the message the ambassadors carry.

The answer is so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God. Paul writes, "God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God." Read it slowly and you see the two sides. The One who knew no sin was made to be sin on our behalf. The purpose is that "…in Him we might become the righteousness of God." That's the text's reason, and I'll leave it as big as Paul wrote it.

The answer is to receive it in vain. Paul writes, "…we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain." In vain means for nothing, like getting handed a fresh batch of cookies and letting them go stale on the counter. I think Paul wants the grace to count for something.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!" He says now, not someday. He's quoting words God says (Isaiah 49:8): "In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you." Paul takes those words and says now is the time.
